title: Film club
titleCn: 电影院电影俱乐部入会咨询

paragraphs.text: Part one.
You will hear a teenager asking about joining a film club.
First, you have some time to look at questions one to four.
Now listen carefully and answer questions one to four.
Hi, can I help you?
Yeah. I saw on the Internet that you have a film club here at the cinema, uh, but there wasn't a lot about it. Can you tell me a bit more?

Yes. We're still setting up the webpage. Sorry about that. We only started the club a few months ago. It's been very popular right from the beginning. We have regular film showings, and there are lots of other benefits.
How often does the club meet?
Um, every two weeks on Thursday nights.
Okay. And I'm 16, so could I join?
Sure. People of any age can join.
Right. Uh, so how much does it cost to join?
Well, it depends. The basic charge is 24 pounds a season, but for people eligible for concessions, it's 21 pounds fifty.
I'm a student.
You'd get the concession rate then.
That's good.
That entitles you to free entry to the club films and also to 2 pounds off tickets for all other films on at the cinema, so you'd pay 4.50 pounds instead of 6.50 pounds.
Great. Okay.
Now, I don't know if this applies to you, but club members are also eligible for 3 hours complimentary parking when there's a film on.
Well, I don't drive, but my girlfriend does, so it might be useful, yes. Okay. Uh, well, I'd definitely like to join.
Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions five to ten.
Now listen and answer questions five to ten.
Can you give me any information about the next few films you're showing?

I'm afraid we've run out of leaflets for this season, so I'll tell you about the next few films, and hopefully we'll have all the details on the Internet soon. So the next meeting's this Thursday, 14th October, and that's a film called Pablo.
Ah, I read the reviews of that. It's set in Argentina, isn't it?
Mm-hmm.
About a child who's run away from home?
That's right. It just came out recently.
And the kid somehow gets on TV, and he wins a dance competition or something.
A singing competition, yeah. I haven't seen it either, but it tells you on the posters. Yes, it sounds really good.
Well, I definitely want to see that. What's on after that?

On 28th October, there's an American film called The Soldier. That's an old silent movie. But in this showing, we have someone who'll accompany it on the piano, just like they used to in the old cinemas, though it was sometimes an organ accompaniment in those days.
Must be a pretty old film then. When did they release the first talkies? Was it 1926 or 1927?
Yes. Well, this was made in 1922, so well before. Though I think they had short feature films with sound by 1923 actually.
So what sort of film is it?
Well, it's billed as a comedy, though you'd think it was a war film from the title. I don't know much about the plot. We don't have much information, but you could always look it up on the Internet.
Yeah, I'll do that.

Then the next film after that, so that'll be, let's see, the 11th November, is a film about animals, and it's just called Tiger, and that's a cartoon film, which makes it sound as if it's for children, but actually it's aimed at adults, and it's really quite frightening in places. I saw it when it first came out.
What's it about?

It's got no humans in it at all. It's just about the effect of environmental changes millions of years ago on the animals who lived then. It's a really strange film. There's a talk afterwards given by the director, so that should be very popular. You'll need to book early for that, I should think.
Right. Well, thanks for all that. Now, if you can give me the application form.
Sure.
That is the end of part one. You now have one minute to check your answers to part one.
